---
title: "Quick start"
---

Attaviz gives you two ways to make charts in the WBG style. Enable the theme,
and every Altair chart you write uses it. Or use a chart template, which also
makes common editorial choices for you.

## Style any Altair chart

Run `attaviz.enable()` once. Every Altair chart after that call uses WBG fonts,
colors, and spacing. You do not need to change your chart code.

```{python}
import altair as alt
import attaviz
import pandas as pd

attaviz.enable()

source = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "site": ["Crookston", "Duluth", "Grand Rapids", "Morris", "University Farm"],
        "yield": [35.1, 33.0, 24.9, 35.4, 32.7],
    }
)

alt.Chart(source, title="Barley yield by site").mark_bar().encode(
    x="yield:Q",
    y="site:N",
)
```

## Use a chart template

A chart template builds a complete chart from summarized data. Pass your data
to a template such as `attaviz.bar()`.

```{python}
attaviz.bar(
    source,
    category="site",
    value="yield",
    title="Barley yield by site",
    subtitle="Mean yield across varieties and years",
)
```

Templates handle recurring editorial choices such as sorting, labels,
tooltips, highlighting, number formatting, and responsive width. They return
ordinary Altair charts, so normal Altair customization remains available.

```python
chart = attaviz.bar(
    source,
    category="site",
    value="yield",
    highlight="Morris",
)

chart = attaviz.frame(
    chart,
    description="Horizontal bars comparing mean barley yield at six sites.",
    source="Minnesota agricultural experiment stations",
)
```

## Size variants

Three typography/spacing presets are available. Pick the one that matches
the intended display width.

```python
attaviz.enable(size="small")   # charts under ~400px wide
attaviz.enable(size="medium")  # 400–700px (default)
attaviz.enable(size="large")   # wider than 700px
```

## Per-chart sizing

To size a single chart without switching the global theme:

```python
chart = attaviz.configure_size(chart, width=600, aspect_ratio="16:9")
```
